title: WhiteMagic Memory Crystals
subtitle: LocalCrystalStore default, commitment kept off the store
label: whitemagic-crystals
measured_on: whitemagic crystal_client.py at 273b177b (sha256 e44b13f2), Python 3.12, macOS
What this means: Every one of the ten edits is refused when the agent next reads, the whole-store rollback and the erasure resurrection included. The shipped LocalCrystalStore keeps its signed, erasure-aware commitment outside the store directory, under XDG_STATE_HOME/whitemagic/anchors, refuses an anchor path inside the store or behind a symlink, and only lets the commitment move forward. The composition engine, chaining storage moves up to two at a time, found no sequence that landed where its single moves did not. The result holds while the anchors directory stays out of the attacker's reach; the in-store row shows what happens when it does not.
Where the attacker stands: The attacker reads and writes the WhiteMagic store directory, as a mounted volume, a shared disk or a restored backup would allow. He holds no signing key. In the default and audit rows he cannot reach the anchors directory under XDG_STATE_HOME; in the in-store row the commitment sits inside the directory he controls. An attacker who holds a key or the anchors directory is a different measurement and these rows do not speak for it.
verdicts_intro:
Detection point: the read path. 10 of the ten edits were refused there, 0 served as genuine, 0 not applicable.

Level L4. What L4 means.
reproduce_intro: Everything runs offline. The run seeds a fresh store through the client's own API, applies each edit beneath it, reopens the store and records what came back.

export AGMI_WHITEMAGIC_CRYSTAL_CLIENT=<path to crystal_client.py>
